section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1973
title: The volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population in States, U. Ts. and Metropolitan cities varies between 3.38 to 68.02. There could be numerous factors responsible for this vast variation between the two. The reasons might be due to the difference in topography of the areas, population, level of industrialisation and other socio-economic factors. The highest number of accidental deaths occurred in the state of Maharashtra (23,601) followed by Madhya Pradesh (13,901), Uttar Pradesh (9,602) and West Bengal (8,863). These four states together accounted for more than 53 per cent of total accidental deaths in the entire country. The volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population was the highest in Maharashtra (44.57) followed by Madhya Pradesh (31.59). Fourteen States recorded volume of accidental deaths below all India average (18.29) with Nagaland (3.38) having the least. Among Union Territories, the volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population was the highest for the Union Territory of Pondicherry (68.02) while it was only 2.94 for Lakshadweep. Among the metropolitan cities, the volume of accidental deaths was the highest for Bombay (67.85). The detailed statistics are presented in Table IV.
